statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low, with cash equities and index futures closed for the entire forecast window.
recommendation: Tail stays well below the block threshold across all 24 forecast hours because every one of them falls inside the CME weekend halt. The elevated Stress reading describes a persistent long-end yield and energy backdrop rather than an observed one-way Nasdaq-100 path. The first opportunity for fresh price-path evidence is the Sunday futures reopen at 22:00Z, which lies outside this window.
headline: Nasdaq-100 weekend halt: Tail low after Friday's record probe mean-reverted; long-end yields and energy keep Stress elevated
body: Friday closed the Nasdaq-100 at 30,807.93, up 1.00% and a record close, after probing an intraday high of 31,017.53 and then giving back roughly 210 points to finish near the session low of 30,737.07. That completed retracement, rather than a shallow pullback or repeated extension, is the last observed price structure. September payrolls of 29,000 against expectations near 90,000, unemployment at 4.2% and average hourly earnings up 0.1% on the month cut priced odds of an October rate hike to about 16% from roughly 64% a week earlier and drove a narrow, tech-led advance, with the Nasdaq-100 ahead of the S&P 500 at 0.74% and the Dow at 0.49%. Nvidia set an intraday record on a 150 billion dollar buyback authorisation. VIX fell about 6.6% to 15.31. The backdrop nevertheless stays difficult: Treasury yields reversed higher despite the soft labour data, with the 2-year at 4.8414% and the 10-year at 5.2939%, the 30-year near 5.61%, Brent at about $102.25 and WTI at about $91.11 after a one-month low of $88.06 and a recovery on G7 emergency reserve plans, while Strait of Hormuz transit remains disrupted. CME equity-index futures closed on Friday at 21:00Z and do not restart until 22:00Z on Sunday, beyond this horizon, so no mechanism for sustained mean-reversion failure exists inside the forecast window. Confidence is high because verified settlement levels, the session range, VIX, the 2-year, 10-year and 30-year curve, energy and the seven-day U.S. calendar are all in hand; the only absent input is a live price path, which is absent by market closure rather than by any gap in research.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover Friday's payroll session and the opening stretch of the weekend halt. Tail held in the watch band through the European morning, rose to 25 and then 27 around the 12:30Z payroll release and the 13:30Z cash open as the index gapped up and extended toward its record, and fell back into the watch band once that advance faded from the intraday high. From 21:00Z, with futures closed, Tail declined steadily from the low twenties to single digits and the mapped state returned to EA_ON, while Stress eased from the high seventies toward the low sixties as realised volatility collapsed. All 24 hourly slots are backed by published Claude assessments; none required an unavailable marker.
outlookSummary: All 24 forecast hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, since index futures closed on Friday at 21:00Z and do not restart until 22:00Z on Sunday, beyond this horizon. With no tradeable session and therefore no mechanism for sustained mean-reversion failure, Tail is projected to hold between 6 and 8 and the mapped state stays EA_ON throughout, with no danger window published. Stress eases from 60 toward 56 through Saturday as realised volatility stays at zero, then firms modestly toward 59 into Sunday morning as the new week's catalyst stack comes into view: ISM Services on 5 October at 14:00Z, FOMC Minutes on 7 October at 18:00Z, two Treasury auctions and jobless claims, all against a 10-year near 5.29%. Confidence decays gently from 86 to 79 purely because the Friday settlement reference ages without replacement. The weekend risk actually being carried is gap risk at the Sunday reopen, which is a single repricing event and is distinct from the sustained one-way path that Tail measures.
